html:
Capital of the Dominican Republic and the oldest European city in the Americas that has been lived in ever since its founding. Christopher Columbus's brother Bartholomew founded it in 1496 on the Ozama River, on the island of Hispaniola. After a hurricane, the governor Nicolás de Ovando rebuilt it on the west bank in 1502.

For a few decades it was the base of the Spanish empire in the Americas. Expeditions to Puerto Rico, Cuba and the mainland set out from here, while the Taíno of the island died from forced labour and disease.

It holds many firsts: the first cathedral in the Americas, the first royal court of appeal and an early university. In 1511 the friar Antonio de Montesinos preached a sermon here against the abuse of the Taíno, which led to the Laws of Burgos.

The city declined once Mexico and Peru drew Spain's attention, and Francis Drake sacked it in 1586. Its colonial quarter is now a World Heritage Site.
